held.why: research skipped: One search for a Three Musketeers Ridge scramble from Snow/Nada Lakes. The only description found places the ridge on the way to Toketie Pass as part of the Edwards Mesa traverse, and it is a Mountaineers page (403). The opened countryhighpoints Enchantments page does not cover it. No route description, timing or gain for the ridge itself. Row issue: the id says big_chiwaukum, but the approach (Snow Lakes, Nada Lake) and the Toketie context put the ridge in the Enchantments, not the Chiwaukums.

research skipped: Two searches. The only 'Northwest Chimney Route' found on Mountain Project, once opened, is on Montezuma's Head in Arizona, not Cascade Peak. Other results cover Mixup Peak and the C-J couloir, plus a 1962 AAJ note on Cascade Peak's history. No source describes a northwest chimney on Cascade Peak.

research skipped: Three searches. The only route-specific source is an OpenBeta mirror of the Mountain Project listing (FA Childs/Goldie 2000, 5.8 IV solo, up to 5.9+ V roped). It returned 404 when opened, and the Mountain Project page itself did not come up. SummitPost (403) has only grade notes. No opened source gives days, hours or distances for the Cedar Creek line. Possible row issue: the row's grade-IV/V ridge is listed with pitches 0 and a 3.5-mile crest, and the snippets suggest a much longer, committing day.

research skipped: One search. The only route-specific result is a 2004 CascadeClimbers inquiry thread (403), which says few parties climb it. No opened source describes the route, timing or camps. Row issue: the id says glacier_peak, but the peak is Mount Rainier.

research skipped: Two searches. Nothing describes a route called Tahoma Cleaver on Rainier. Results cover Success Cleaver, the Tahoma Glacier and the DC. The only mention is the Mountaineers Glacier Island Traverse page (403 domain, seen only as a snippet), which reaches the cleaver's base at about 8,100 ft. Row issue: the id says glacier_peak, but the peak is Mount Rainier.

research skipped: One search, three pages opened. The Mountain Project page describes the headwall (Grade II, 2,000 ft, Riley trailhead, descend the West Ridge) but gives no times, distances or camps. The Oregon Hikers report follows the same Riley Creek approach only to the moraine lakes, as a day hike; it does not climb the headwall. The turns-all-year report saw the headwall from above and skied the west ridge instead. That leaves one source for the climb itself and no stated hours.

research skipped: One search, two pages opened. climberkyle climbed Switchback's southeast ridge from Crater Creek via Cooney Lake. yellowleaf went from Martin Creek via Cooney Lake and passed Boiling Lake only on day 2. Neither describes the west ridge or west face from Boiling Lake. The Mountaineers route page that does describe it is 403 (snippet only).

research skipped: One search, two pages opened. The detailed South Face reports (approach of about 6 to 7 hours up Ingalls and Crystal Creeks, a tarn camp, 3 pitches) are all SummitPost pages (403). Lemke's page has only the summit date and grade. The Wenatchee Outdoors page is a ski tour from the Enchantments side and says the south side is for climbers only. No second openable source.

research skipped: Two searches (North Ridge trip reports; north ridge 5.6 via Cliff/Bluff Lake). Every Chaval result covered the West Route, the west face or the west ridge, mostly on SummitPost and CascadeClimbers (403) or in a WTA trip report (403). No reachable page describes a North Ridge on Mount Chaval, so its grade, pitches and timing cannot be confirmed.

research skipped: One search and one opened source (Steph Abegg, Mystery Ridge enchainment). It confirms the ridge as a descent from Crowder's summit to a heather camp at Pickell Pass (third-class ledges, some fourth-class moves, a rappel near the base, a chasm splitting the lower ridge). But it gives only a whole-day total for a multi-peak traverse day, with no figures for this ridge. Every other result was a CascadeClimbers report (403). One source, and that one describing a traverse, is not enough for a stand-alone plan.
low confidence

research skipped: One search and one opened source (an Alpine Institute NW Rib route profile). It names the NE Ridge of the summit pyramid (5.7) only as one of two ways to finish from the Upper Curtis Glacier after the NW Rib, with no days, camps or times for it. Other results covered the Sulphide or Fisher Chimneys routes or were on 403 sites. The ridge is a finish to other climbs, not a trip of its own, and no second source describes it.

research skipped: One search for the Northeast Ridge of Silver Star's west summit. Results confirm only its listing as Grade III 5.9 on SummitPost (403), plus trip reports for the Silver Star Glacier route via Burgundy Col (Mountaineers, 403). No reachable page describes the ridge's pitches, time on route or descent, so a plan would be the glacier route's plan with an invented ridge day.

research skipped: One search. Only the Mountain Project area listing (5.7 M5-, mixed, one star) describes the route. No reachable page gives an approach time, a descent or a car-to-car figure, or anything beyond the shared New York Gully approach. One thin source is not enough.

research skipped: One search for Spectre Peak's Haunted Wall returned nothing about the climb at all. No reachable source describes the route, and the row holds no waypoints or figures to check against.

research skipped: One search, plus the Mountain Project area page opened. The area lists only Slippery Slab Tower's NE Face, and Thunder Mountain's documented route is the SE-slope scramble from Upper Thunder Lake. No reachable source describes a North Face route, so none of its figures can be sourced.

research skipped: Searched again for a North Mowich Headwall climb. The opened sources (a 2012 blog and a 2012 turns-all-year report) and the new search results all describe the central Mowich Face, or a party that found the headwall icefall out of shape and went around it. No opened page climbs the North Mowich Headwall itself, and the only route pages (SummitPost, CascadeClimbers) return 403. The day figures in the earlier plan were derived, not stated.

research skipped: Searched for a second NW ridge source. The opened pages (ahelwer 2017 and 2018, lemkeclimbs, whereiskylemiller, plus the earlier hippohamster and Wenatchee Outdoors pages) describe the NE ridge, the SW ridge, a ski descent of the NW face, or a Colchuck-side scramble. None covers the NW ridge from the Stuart Lake trail. The only NW ridge reports (Mountaineers 2016 and 2025, CascadeClimbers 2013, a SummitPost log) return 403. No opened source gives hours, miles or gain for this line. Row note: high_point_ft is null while the summit waypoint is labeled as a NE Ridge point.

research skipped: Searched again for the 1976 Bard/Chouinard/Cunningham East Face. The opened AAJ pages mention it only in passing, and Mountain Project covers neighbouring lines (South Buttress, The Swarm). The only route descriptions (SummitPost East Face pages, CascadeClimbers) return 403, and one SummitPost snippet gives 12 pitches rather than 6, so even the route length is unsettled. No source gives hours, and the earlier plan derived its gain and miles. Row issue: the row's gain_ft of 2,500 is less than its own pullout-to-summit rise (5,227 to 8,066 ft), and its dist_km of 2 is shorter than the roughly 2 mi one way given for the approach.

research skipped: OpenBeta's page for Western Dihedral has only the grade and the 2017 FA; the mirror that appears to hold the description returned 404. Mountain Project's Squire Creek Wall page does not list the route. The one opened approach source (climberkyle) covers only the shared walk to the grassy saddle. research skipped: Searched for Northwest Ridge trip reports and opened stevensong (no report reached) and sverdina Big_Four1 (a Dry Creek attempt). The only NW Ridge mention is a 2007 SummitPost climbers' log seen as a snippet (403). No opened source describes this route.

research skipped: The same Big Four searches (AAJ north face notes, sverdina, stevensong, turns-all-year) turned up nothing on the Tower Route beyond a SummitPost access note (403). No opened source gives its line, timing or descent.

research skipped: A search for a Hester Lake southwest-ridge ascent found only a turns-all-year line noting a possible southwest-side descent into the Hester bowl, plus Hester Lake approach notes for Mount Price. The SummitPost 'Southwest Ridge' results are for an Idaho peak. No report of this route was found.

research skipped: A search for East Buttress reports returned only Northeast Ridge and South Route reports and the SummitPost peak page (403), which is the only description of the East Buttress (from Wing Lake, gully system, class 3-4). There is no second source.

research skipped: A search on the north ridge from the Middle Fork found only first-ascent history (Wikipedia, June 1971) and Yellowleaf trips from the Chikamin/Iceberg side via the NE ridge. No source describes the north ridge climb or the river crossing.

research skipped: A search for a Harts Pass/PCT ascent found PCT and Castle Pass hike pages and SummitPost log snippets (403) describing the west ridge from Castle Pass and a south-face descent. Neither matches this row's Castle Creek basin, northeast gully and notch line, and no opened source gives timing for it.

research skipped: No new search, since the budget went to routes with better odds. Earlier work found only first-ascent material from a party approaching from Canada, and nothing on the lawful Ross Lake / Freezeout Creek approach.

research skipped: A search for Chair-Bryant traverse reports found only the OpenBeta entry (the stg.openbeta.io page returns 404 on fetch), a 2004 CascadeClimbers note (403) on going Bryant to Chair, and Chair Peak circumnavigation ski reports. No opened source gives timing or a day structure.
research skipped: No new search. Earlier work found no source describing the East Face (the row's own descent is 'presumed'), and northern Pickets material covers other routes.
research skipped: No new search. The only known source is the 1988 AAJ note, which gives no approach, camps or descent. A second source 404'd earlier and SummitPost returns 403.

research skipped: No new search. The AAJ 2009 and Alpinist 2008 first-ascent reports describe the route, but give no mileage, gain or hours for the two approach days or the walk-out, so those days would carry no sourced figure. The two also disagree on length (29 vs 25 pitches).

research skipped: A search for a 'northeast face' route on Fortress found the East Route, the East Ridge and Chiwawa Mountain material (SummitPost 403, wenatcheeoutdoors, AAJ Chiwawa 'Intravenous'). Nothing names or describes a Northeast Face line on Fortress.

research skipped: A search for North Peak South Ridge found only a Wikipedia route list (class 3-4 South Ridge, ambiguous between peaks). I opened the stevensong report: it climbs the Northwest Ridge from Manning Park in one day, not this route. The other reports cover the NE ridge/buttress, the SW buttress and the north face.

research skipped: A search for Tank Lakes / northeast shoulder found Alpine Lakes High Route reports (WTA 403, climberkyle, Lemke) and Yellowleaf traverses. These mention a narrow NE ridge passage and other lines but describe no ascent of the northeast shoulder with camps or per-day figures.

research skipped: A search for Crowder via Easy Ridge found Abegg's Mystery Ridge enchainment (Crowder's southwest flank reached from Wild Lake, to the south) and a climberkyle traverse that bypassed Crowder on its west side. The other hits were CascadeClimbers (403). Nothing climbs this route from the row's Easy Ridge / Perfect Pass approach.

research skipped: A search for 'Harniss' chute with Mount Lincoln and Flapjack Lakes found no mention of the chute anywhere. The hits were Flapjack Lakes hike notes, a Mildred Lakes approach to Lincoln, and an unrelated Lincoln Peak (Baker). The route name could not be confirmed.

research skipped: Retry did not search further: the prior pass found only a one-line Mountain Project mention of this north-face line, and the route has no published grade, length, approach or descent anywhere open. Searches were saved for routes with better odds. Still no source.

research skipped: Searched for Mount Seattle Noyes Basin from Low Divide. Results were SummitPost 2010 Christie/Noyes/Meany reports (403), a Mazamas activity page about Seattle Creek basin and the Noyes-Seattle ridge (a different line), and Lists of John stats. No open page describes ascending Mount Seattle through Noyes Basin with times or figures.

research skipped: Not searched again: the prior pass covered the open Sefrit reports (onehikeaweek, turns-all-year), and both use the Nooksack Cirque side. The only pages that name Bloody Head Couloir are SummitPost and CascadeClimbers, which return 403. Still no source.

research skipped: Searched for West Twin Needle from the Himmelhorn notch. Hits were Abegg's Twin Needles report (from Eye Col, a different line), a 2018 Southern Pickets enchainment report on CascadeClimbers (403) calling West Twin easy third class as part of a traverse, an AAC article on a Himmelhorn notch pitch, and Holsten's traverse blog. None gives a standalone West Slope ascent with days, times or figures.

research skipped: Searched for Golden Horn north and northeast routes. Only the 1958 AAJ note describes the North Face, and it gives no figures. Other hits (Lemke, Yellowleaf, WTA, Mountaineers) cover the standard south-side scramble from Snowy Lakes. No second source.

research skipped: Searched for Golden Horn NE Arete 5.8. The one route report (skisickness 2011, including its ?view=print URL) still returns 404. Alpinist covers a different new route on Golden Horn. Snippets confirm the 1979 Skoog-Walseth first ascent and that the climb is loose, but no opened page describes the arete's day.

research skipped: Searched for the Hozomeen South Peak SE Buttress via Willow Lake. The 1989 AAJ first-ascent report is still the only account, and it gives no descent or exit. Wikipedia lists only grade and FA party, and it places the route under the Southwest sub-peak, which conflicts with the row. The SummitPost and CascadeClimbers pages for the south peaks return 403. No second source.

research skipped: Not searched again. Mountain Project and Abegg are already known: they give 4 pitches, a 60 m rappel from P3 and a 37 min to 1 h east-face approach. Neither states a full-day time, distance or gain for this climb, so no day figure can be sourced without computing one.

research skipped: Searched for Shuksan Northwest Arete AAJ and White Salmon. Hits were the 2007 Northwest Arayete (a different 5.9 line), the Northwest Rib (AAI), and a 2009 CascadeClimbers Northwest Arete report (403). There is no AAJ entry for this arete and no open page with its days or camps.

research skipped: Not searched again: no source describes a West Ridge route on Snoqualmie Mountain, and the row has no grade or description.

research skipped: Searched for The Incisor in Royal Basin. Every hit was another Incisor (Combatant Mountain BC, Montana, Australia), and the one Olympic report is on CascadeClimbers (403). No open source.

Stevensong's Tooth page was opened but holds no route text in its index. Snippets say the north side is a class 3-4 scramble used mostly as a descent, but no opened page describes ascending it with times or figures.
